family_nodes.name: Exclusion hypotheses with cheapest falsifiers
sources: Jeremy, 2026-11-13: an exclusion is a hypothesis, not a fact
family_nodes.source_evidence: Offline fixtures only; no model campaign.
process: Seats from several model families propose exclusions, each with a falsifier and its cost
The host counts agreement by model family: disagreement is frontier, one family is uncorroborated, several agreeing families are probably dead
Falsifiers run frontier first, then uncorroborated, then probably-dead ones no dearer than the dead floor, under one retest budget
A refuted exclusion reopens its branch; the solver sees only open branches
Control arm: the same task with retests off
math: seats of one family are one vote, because shared training makes their errors correlated
an exclusion with no falsifier is refused before any test runs
a no-root claim is checked by exhaustive scan of the open branches, so the control arm's typed refusal is lawful but can hide the answer
family_nodes.host_check: exact polynomial evaluation of each falsifier and of the answer

team.goal: Spend test effort where model families disagree, and still test cheap dead branches.

roles.task: Vote on exclusions and name the cheapest falsifier for each.
Solve inside the open branches.
Deterministic check; the only component that can accept. Never a model.

boost.action: a refuted exclusion reopens its branch

family_nodes.name: Failure ledger with trial-gated rules
sources: Jeremy, 2026-11-14: Python checks nothing; failures must persist and be reused across runs
family_nodes.source_evidence: Offline fixtures only; no model campaign.
process: The host replays the ledger's hash chain and lists the rules already admitted
The host judges each reported failure itself and writes its record; a correct answer cannot be recorded as a failure
A model proposes one rule from the recorded failures
Each held-out case is answered twice: without the proposed rule and with it
The host judges both answers of every case and writes the trial record
The ledger admits the rule only on that trial; the next run loads every admitted rule
math: admit iff treated_correct > baseline_correct and clean_panel_hits = 0, on the rule's latest trial
clean_panel_hits = number of held-out cases the baseline answered correctly and the treated run did not
held out: the trial's case ids share nothing with the failures the rule was derived from
entry hash = SHA-256(domain line, seq, previous hash, record), so an edited, reordered or cut ledger does not replay
family_nodes.host_check: Rust ledger admission on a trial the host judged itself (pfp_operad witness, trial, ledger)

team.goal: Rules that are loaded in later runs only after they fixed held-out cases and broke none.

roles.task: Propose one rule from the recorded failures.
Answer every held-out case without the rule and with it.
Deterministic check; the only component that can accept. Never a model.

boost.action: a rejected rule stays in the ledger and can be tried again in a later run

family_nodes.name: Host-run operad candidates
sources: docs/plans/operads_redesign.md slice 2d: a candidate with a body the host can run
family_nodes.source_evidence: Offline fixtures only; no model campaign.
process: One reply gives candidates and an answer; each candidate names source colours, a target colour and a body from the host's closed list
The host types every candidate by the canon's task value colours
The host runs each candidate that has a body on the task's case and on sealed probe cases
The host compares each result with its own judge's result; the caller supplies no expected value
The host judges the answer
math: HOST_VERIFIED(c) iff body(c) is in the closed list and eval(c, x) = f(x) for every case x, with f the host judge
REFUSED(c) iff c is ill typed, its id repeats, or eval(c, x) != f(x) for some case x it fits
certified iff some candidate is HOST_VERIFIED, none is REFUSED and the answer equals f(x0) on the task's case x0
probes: cases the prompt never carries, so a body that agrees on x0 by coincidence is still refused
family_nodes.host_check: Rust run of each candidate body against the host's own judge (pfp_operad run, judge)

team.goal: An accepted answer together with an operation the host ran itself and found to give the same result.

roles.task: Answer the task and name the operation used, with a body from the closed list.
Deterministic check; the only component that can accept. Never a model.

boost.action: none; a refused run is reported with the host's code for each candidate

family_nodes.name: Host-tested patch repair
sources: docs/plans/operads_redesign.md slice 3: a supplied patch tested by the host on a working copy
family_nodes.source_evidence: Offline fixtures only; no model campaign.
process: One reply gives a unified diff for files in the task's write set
The host verifies each declared file against its SHA-256 and copies the files to a new run folder
The host runs every check command on the copy and records each exit code
The host applies the patch to the copy, only inside the write set and only where each hunk fits exactly
The host runs every check again and compares the checks that fail before and after
The host confirms the declared files still have their declared hashes
A patch that was tested and did not repair leaves a failure record, which the host appends to the failure ledger
math: F0 = the checks with a nonzero exit before the patch, F1 = the checks with a nonzero exit after it
outcome, tested in this order: NO_REPAIR_NEEDED iff F0 is empty; REGRESSION iff F1 is not a subset of F0; REPAIRED iff F1 is empty; PARTIAL iff |F1| < |F0|; else INEFFECTIVE
certified iff the outcome is REPAIRED and every declared file still has its declared SHA-256
failure class: StructuralNonFit for a patch that is malformed or outside the write set, BoundaryLeakage on REGRESSION, CounterfeitExactness on PARTIAL or INEFFECTIVE
family_nodes.host_check: Rust test of a supplied patch on a working copy, by the task's check commands before and after (pfp_operad repair)

team.goal: A patch the host applied to a copy of the task's files and found to make every failing check pass without breaking a passing one.

roles.task: Write one unified diff for the files in the write set.
Deterministic check; the only component that can accept. Never a model.

boost.action: none; a patch that did not repair is recorded in the failure ledger with the host's class

findings.finding: Only WF1-WF5 have public family runners; WF6-WF49 are documented proposals. Nested historical sources are not absent, but do not make the proposed family design executable as published.

No inventoried existing workflow supplies a verified checker for every obligation of the unchanged grad-QM seed. WF1-WF3 can transport schema_only; WF4 demands integer_sum_v1 and WF5 recognizes only a complete finite exact-sum language.

Historical pilot imports require omega_engine_* private/runtime owners; relabelled names and paths may invalidate retained hashes. Source presence and historical receipts do not prove portable replay.

The cleaned checkout includes the retired finite-QM programme, absent at the initial audit base. Its P0-P5 contracts explicitly retain unreviewed obligations and require task-applicable independent checkers; source/layout/provider dependencies remain.

Challenge documentation discloses C027 dual-check limit, C049 independent checker accepting 31/48 mutants, C041 external Lean dependency, C052 missing package tests, and C058 sampled rather than exhaustive checking above 8 bits. These are disclosed historical/current-source limits, not newly reproduced test results.
WF26 and WF27 historical improvements used answer-leaking/full-repair hints; WF28 and WF48 include reference self-scores. Do not pool them with independent model accuracy.

The older finite-QM prompt compiler prints computed expected values and requests JSON extraction; its gate engine matches expected certificates and some failure strings include expected values. This is extraction/finite-control checking, not blind derivation, and cannot supply answer-free repair feedback unchanged. The nested v3 programme expressly supersedes the legacy exercises.
C001 attention-mask pipeline declares tokenizer_json_sha256 and prompt_template_digest UNSET; its pin note explicitly says NOT_READY. A pipeline file is not evidence of a ready experiment.

finite_composition_recommendation.principle: Enumerate typed finite programmes, not all 49! orderings. A workflow family, task preset, checker-development activity, campaign and harness gate have different input/output types.
finite_composition_recommendation.production: Programme := FreezeTask ; OptionalGuidance ; CandidateStage ; Check ; BoundedRepair? ; OptionalChallenge ; Record

finite_controls.max_agents: bounded; later ten research agents are planning roles, not automatic independent solvers
finite_controls.max_stage_orderings: topological orders of selected typed dependency graph

validity_constraints: Freeze seed bytes/hash, target semantics, assumptions, checker pins, evaluation policy and budgets before dispatch.
Each composition edge matches complete input/output schemas and domain hypotheses; source_dependency edges do not by themselves license execution.
Task-specific presets require a checked adapter; retain inapplicable statuses rather than silently translate the benchmark.
Only checked reversible representations may count as same-seed dialects; constraint changes and changed claims are separate tasks.
Keep schema acceptance, finite checks, symbolic identities, numerical sanity checks and mathematical proof review distinct.
Mining/challenge proposals never see private answer keys; residual feedback uses bounded failure classes and excludes expected values.
Freeze isolated proposals before sharing; agreement is not an independent mathematical judge.
Unroll bounded repairs/re-entry into attempt-indexed DAG nodes; never reset the root budget or hide failed attempts.
Normalize equivalent schedules and identity wrappers; require at least one substantive workflow difference to call a permutation nontrivial.
Campaign/held-out/transfer claims require separate preregistered populations; repeated use of one seed supports only scoped within-item comparisons.

remaining_work: Semantic review remains for every file whose ledger content_reviewed is false; prioritize active runner/checker/test sources over historical raw replies.
Resolve historical/private-runtime imports and source-layout dependencies before labelling any nested pilot portable or executable.
Independently assess each candidate QM adapter and test plan without reading the benchmark private key.
Complete remote campaign source/test review; the present pass fully read its top-level public contracts only.
Check declared source references against owning papers/code and distinguish reproduced tests from documented receipts.
